title: Where antiviral drugs act in a virus life cycle
ariaLabel: Schematic of three antiviral targets: the viral DNA polymerase of herpes viruses, the neuraminidase that releases influenza virus from the cell, and the RNA polymerase of RNA viruses. Aciclovir-type drugs block viral DNA copying, oseltamivir-type drugs block release of new virus, and remdesivir-type drugs block viral RNA copying.
caption: Schematic, not to scale. Flow and levels are qualitative and illustrative; no dose, concentration or lipid value is shown or implied.
blockInfo: A drug of the chosen class acting at this step (generic teaching symbol, not a named drug's shape). Less passes here, with the effects shown at the cholesterol and the LDL receptors.

nodes.label: Herpes viral DNA
nodes.info: The genome of a herpes virus (for example herpes simplex or varicella zoster) in an infected cell.

nodes.label: New influenza virus
nodes.info: New influenza viruses at the surface of an infected cell, still attached to it.

nodes.label: Virus released
nodes.info: Virus freed to infect new cells.

nodes.label: Viral RNA genome
nodes.info: The genome of an RNA virus in an infected cell.

nodes.label: Virus spread
nodes.info: A teaching score for how well virus keeps being made and released in the cells it infects.

edges.label: viral DNA polymerase
edges.info: Aciclovir-type drugs are first activated by a viral enzyme (thymidine kinase) and then block the viral DNA polymerase, so viral DNA is not copied.
Adds to the effect shown at the right.

edges.label: neuraminidase
edges.info: Influenza neuraminidase cuts the new virus free from the cell. Oseltamivir-type drugs block it, so new virus stays stuck and spreads less.
Adds to the effect shown at the right.

edges.label: viral RNA polymerase
edges.info: Nucleotide-analogue drugs (for example remdesivir) are built into viral RNA and stop its copying by the viral RNA polymerase.
Adds to the effect shown at the right.

sources: Where each class acts. Aciclovir-type drugs are activated by viral thymidine kinase and block viral DNA polymerase, oseltamivir-type drugs block neuraminidase, and remdesivir-type drugs block viral RNA polymerase. This is standard teaching in the pharmacology texts the PrepNucleus lessons cite (Katzung; KD Tripathi) and were not checked against a linked source here, so they are flagged for review.
simplified: Antiretrovirals (drawn in their own figure), hepatitis B and C drugs, protease inhibitors, foscarnet, resistance, timing of treatment, who benefits, adverse effects and drug interactions are left out. Virus spread is drawn as a teaching score. Levels and the size of each effect are illustrative. The drug choices are teaching toggles of a class: no named drug, dose or schedule is shown or implied, and the figure does not say who should or should not take any of them.
